messages.content: I got the Dallas answers. It’s Plano, not Las Colinas. The walkthrough is Monday at 3:00 now, and they want me there for setup, not just a quick hello. Training wraps Thursday around 4:30. Can we land on the flight/hotel combo?

Yes. The 3:00 setup changes the outbound: I would not use the afternoon DEN-DFW options because they put you on the ground after 4 or leave no cushion. Best pairing: United nonstop DEN-DFW late morning, about 10:05 a.m.-1:05 p.m., then go straight to the Plano site. It costs more than the one-stop, but it protects the setup. Cheaper alternative: one stop through Houston or Austin, arriving about 1:50-2:05, saving roughly $90-$120, but the 45-55 minute connection means any delay could make you miss the walkthrough. Hotel choice narrows to Hilton Dallas/Plano Granite Park: around $218 pre-tax, strong reviews, pool and fitness center, no hot tub, 8-12 minutes from the site. The suite-style option with pool, hot tub, and fitness is more like 20-25 minutes away in traffic. My recommendation is the late-morning nonstop plus Hilton Granite Park.
I do not love leaving before lunch, but missing a 3:00 setup would be worse. Is arriving around 1:05 actually enough time if I have the demo kit?

Enough, but only if the demo kit stays carry-on and you do not stop at the hotel first. Plan on 10-15 minutes to deplane, 5-10 to get to pickup, and 30-45 minutes to Plano depending on traffic. That puts you at the site roughly 2:00-2:20 on a normal day. If you check equipment, the buffer shrinks too much.
Carry-on demo kit only. I can check in at the hotel after the walkthrough. What about the cheaper connection?

I would pass on it for this trip. The one-stop price is attractive, but the connection is the fragile part, not the total travel time. If the first leg leaves Denver 20 minutes late, you are either sprinting in the hub or arriving in Dallas right when you should be walking into setup. It is a reasonable leisure fare, not a good fixed-client-meeting fare.
Fair. Use the nonstop. For Thursday, I want enough time after the training ends but not a red-eye.

Then take the Thursday evening nonstop around 7:25 p.m. from DFW to Denver. If training ends around 4:30, you have time to pack up, get to DFW, return a rental or rideshare, and clear security without sitting around all night.
And you would take Hilton even though it is missing the hot tub?

Yes. For this one, the commute matters more. Hilton Granite Park is the better work-trip fit: better location, strong rating, under the $225 pre-tax cap, pool and fitness center, and easy food options nearby. The farther suite hotel wins on recovery amenities because it has the hot tub, but it adds a longer drive each morning and after training. I would only switch to it if the client confirms the commute is reliably under 20 minutes or if you want the suite space more than the shorter drive.
Okay, bookable plan then. Include seat, cancellation, and any commute notes so I can just act on it.

Book this: Monday DEN-DFW late-morning nonstop, about 10:05 a.m.-1:05 p.m.; choose economy/main cabin and grab a window seat if one is open. Do not check the demo kit. Go directly from DFW to the Plano site for the 3:00 walkthrough. Return Thursday on the 7:25-ish p.m. DFW-DEN nonstop. Hotel: Hilton Dallas/Plano Granite Park, Monday through Thursday, cancellable king room, rate around $218 pre-tax; note pool and fitness, no hot tub. After booking, send the client your ETA, ask for parking/loading instructions, and put the hotel cancellation deadline on your calendar.

messages.content: The Dallas plan is already booked, and now the client added a Friday 9:00 a.m. debrief with the regional medical director. My Thursday evening return misses it. What is the least annoying fix?

The practical fix is to stay one more night and move the return to Friday early afternoon. I would not change hotels for one night. Your Hilton can extend, but the extra night is showing about $236 pre-tax, which is above the $225 cap you were using. The flight change looks like no change fee, but about $80-$95 fare difference. Nearby cheaper hotels save maybe $30-$45 but have weaker reviews or drop the pool/fitness setup, and moving would cost time. The only cheaper route is asking them to move the debrief to Thursday late afternoon.
The debrief is 9 to 10 in Plano. Is a noon flight too close?

A noon departure is too tight. You would leave Plano around 10:05, fight traffic to DFW, return the car or get dropped off, and have almost no security cushion. I would target a DFW-DEN nonstop around 1:25 or later.
Can I make the case that they should pay the hotel overage?
Yes. This is client-driven scope after ticketing: added Friday meeting, extra hotel night, and fare difference. Keeping the same hotel also protects the morning schedule and avoids a room move.
Do we still keep the Hilton even without the hot tub?
Yes. For one added night, the short Plano commute beats switching for amenities. The alternatives either add drive time Friday morning or are less solid on reviews.
Draft the note I send for approval.

Suggested note: "The Friday 9:00 a.m. debrief requires me to remain in Plano Thursday night and change my return from Thursday evening to Friday afternoon. The cleanest option is to extend the existing Hilton Dallas/Plano Granite Park reservation one night at approximately $236 pre-tax and move the DFW-DEN nonstop to Friday around 1:25 p.m.; estimated fare difference is $80-$95. This avoids a hotel move, protects the morning debrief, and keeps me close to the site. Please confirm approval for the hotel rate over the $225 cap and the flight change cost."

messages.content: Switching away from work travel for a minute: we need Chicago flights for Thanksgiving week. My husband and I can leave Denver after work Wednesday and need to be back Sunday evening. We’ll stay with family in the suburbs, unless a late arrival makes the first night stupid.
Got it. Which suburb or airport is easiest, and what date is the Wednesday? Also, does after work mean no Denver departure before about 5 p.m.?
Arlington Heights, so ORD is best. Wednesday Nov 25, return Sunday Nov 29. Please use after 5 p.m. out of DEN. Two adults, economy.

I’d rank the flight choices like this: 1) United nonstop DEN-ORD about 6:35-10:00 p.m., returning Sunday about 6:10-7:45 p.m., roughly $560 per person. Cleanest and best timing, but expensive. 2) Nonstop DEN-ORD about 8:25-11:55 p.m., Sunday evening return, about $430 per person. Still simple, but pushes the pickup or hotel question. 3) Southwest or another nonstop to MDW late, arriving near 1:00 a.m., often $350-$375 per person, but MDW is the wrong side for Arlington Heights. 4) One-stop via MSP, MCI, or OMA, $310-$340 per person, but holiday-week short connections are the risk.
The nonstop prices hurt. Are the one-stops mostly one short layover?

Yes, most of the cheaper ones are one stop with 45-65 minute connections. On an ordinary week I’d call that doable; on the night before Thanksgiving, a short connection can turn a small delay into an overnight misconnect because later seats are full. If you consider one, I’d only use a 90-minute-plus connection, and those arrive very late anyway.
I do not want us stranded in Minneapolis to save a couple hundred dollars. What about the 11:55 p.m. ORD arrival?

That is the middle ground. You avoid connection risk and keep the fare lower than the 6:35 p.m. nonstop. The question is whether family will pick you up close to midnight. If not, an ORD airport hotel for one night keeps it sane, then you go to Arlington Heights Thursday morning.
Assume my brother says no pickups after 10:30. Does the airport hotel kill the savings?

For two people, not completely. Rough math: the 6:35 nonstop is about $1,120 total and likely no hotel if he picks you up at 10. The 8:25 nonstop is about $860 total; add $150-$175 for an ORD hotel and maybe a short rideshare, and you land around $1,035-$1,060. So it still saves a bit and avoids a midnight family pickup. MDW stays cheaper but adds a much worse late-night transfer.
Which ORD hotel would be the placeholder? I do not need a hot tub for one night, just clean and shuttle.

Use Hampton Inn Chicago-O’Hare/Schiller Park or Hyatt Place Chicago/O’Hare as placeholders. Both are typically in the $145-$170 range, have airport shuttle service, decent ratings, and enough basics for a late arrival. I’d make it cancellable so you can drop it if your brother decides the late pickup is fine.
Okay, give me the saveable shortlist. No booking until I check with him.

Saveable Chicago shortlist: Dates: Wed Nov 25 after 5 p.m. DEN-ORD, return Sun Nov 29 evening, two adults, economy, Arlington Heights family stay. Top pick: 8:25-ish p.m. nonstop DEN-ORD arriving around 11:55 p.m., with a cancellable ORD airport hotel held for the first night. Backup if pickup at 10 p.m. is available and fare is acceptable: 6:35-ish p.m. nonstop. Avoid the cheap one-stop holiday options unless the layover is at least 90 minutes and the savings are much larger. Hotel placeholder: cancellable Hampton Inn Chicago-O’Hare/Schiller Park or Hyatt Place Chicago/O’Hare; cancel if family pickup works.
